raw: Act 4, Scene 1 — Friar Lawrence’s Cell

sentences.en: Friar Lawrence’s Cell
sentences.ko: 로런스 신부의 수도실

summary.en: Juliet goes to Friar Lawrence for help. He gives her a potion that will make her look dead, so she can escape and join Romeo.
summary.ko: 줄리엣은 로런스 신부에게 도움을 청한다. 신부는 죽은 것처럼 보이게 하는 물약을 주어, 줄리엣이 도망쳐 로미오에게 갈 수 있게 한다.

raw: Enter Friar Lawrence and Paris.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: On Thursday, sir? The time is very short.

sentences.en: On Thursday, sir?
sentences.ko: 목요일이라고요, 백작님?

sentences.en: The time is very short.
sentences.ko: 시간이 너무 촉박하네요.

speaker: PARIS
raw:
My father Capulet will have it so;
And I am nothing slow to slack his haste.

sentences.en: My father Capulet wants it this way.
sentences.ko: 장인어른이 되실 캐퓰릿 경이 그렇게 원하세요.

sentences.en: And I will not slow him down.
sentences.ko: 저도 그분의 서두름을 늦출 생각은 없고요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
You say you do not know the lady’s mind.
Uneven is the course; I like it not.

sentences.en: You say you do not know the lady's mind.
sentences.ko: 백작님은 아가씨의 마음을 모른다고 하셨지요.

sentences.en: This is not the right way to do things.
sentences.ko: 일이 순서가 맞지 않아요.

sentences.en: I do not like it.
sentences.ko: 저는 마음에 들지 않아요.

speaker: PARIS
raw:
Immoderately she weeps for Tybalt’s death,
And therefore have I little talk’d of love;
For Venus smiles not in a house of tears.
Now, sir, her father counts it dangerous
That she do give her sorrow so much sway;
And in his wisdom, hastes our marriage,
To stop the inundation of her tears,
Which, too much minded by herself alone,
May be put from her by society.
Now do you know the reason of this haste.

sentences.en: She cries too much for Tybalt's death.
sentences.ko: 그녀는 티볼트의 죽음 때문에 너무 많이 울어요.

sentences.en: Therefore, I have hardly talked about love.
sentences.ko: 그래서 저는 사랑에 대해 거의 말하지 않았어요.

sentences.en: Love does not smile in a house of tears.
sentences.ko: 눈물 가득한 집에는 사랑이 찾아오지 않거든요.

sentences.en: Now, sir, her father thinks it is dangerous.
sentences.ko: 그런데 신부님, 그분의 아버지께서는 위험하다고 생각하세요.

sentences.en: He thinks she lets her sadness control her too much.
sentences.ko: 그녀가 슬픔에 너무 깊이 빠져 있다고 생각하시죠.

sentences.en: In his wisdom, he hurries our marriage.
sentences.ko: 그분의 지혜로, 결혼을 서두르시는 거예요.

sentences.en: He wants to stop the flow of her tears.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 눈물을 멈추게 하고 싶어 하시거든요.

sentences.en: Alone, she thinks about it too much; with company, she may forget it.
sentences.ko: 혼자 있으면 너무 깊이 생각하지만, 사람들과 함께 있으면 잊을 수도 있으니까요.

sentences.en: Now do you know the reason for this haste?
sentences.ko: 이제 왜 이렇게 서둘러야 하는지 아시겠어요?

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
I would I knew not why it should be slow’d.—
Look, sir, here comes the lady toward my cell.

sentences.en: I wish I did not know why it should be delayed.
sentences.ko: 왜 늦춰야 하는지 내가 몰랐으면 좋으련만.

sentences.en: Look, sir, here comes the lady toward my cell.
sentences.ko: 보세요, 백작님, 아가씨가 이리로 오네요.

raw: Enter Juliet.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Happily met, my lady and my wife!

sentences.en: I am happy to meet you, my lady and my wife!
sentences.ko: 마침 잘 만났어요, 나의 아가씨, 나의 아내여!

speaker: JULIET
raw: That may be, sir, when I may be a wife.

sentences.en: That may be true, sir, when I am a wife.
sentences.ko: 그럴지도 모르죠, 제가 아내가 된다면요.

speaker: PARIS
raw: That may be, must be, love, on Thursday next.

sentences.en: That may be, it must be, love, next Thursday.
sentences.ko: 그럴 거예요, 반드시 그래야 하고요, 내 사랑, 다음 목요일에.

speaker: JULIET
raw: What must be shall be.

sentences.en: What must happen will happen.
sentences.ko: 일어날 일은 일어나겠지요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: That’s a certain text.

sentences.en: That is certainly true.
sentences.ko: 그건 확실한 말씀이지.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Come you to make confession to this father?

sentences.en: Do you come to confess to this priest?
sentences.ko: 이 신부님께 고해하러 오셨나요?

speaker: JULIET
raw: To answer that, I should confess to you.

sentences.en: To answer that, I would have to confess to you.
sentences.ko: 그 질문에 대답하면, 당신에게 고해하는 셈이 되겠네요.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Do not deny to him that you love me.

sentences.en: Do not deny your love for me to him.
sentences.ko: 신부님께 나를 사랑한다는 걸 부인하지 마세요.

speaker: JULIET
raw: I will confess to you that I love him.

sentences.en: I will confess to you that I love him.
sentences.ko: 당신에게 고백하죠, 저는 그분을 사랑해요.

speaker: PARIS
raw: So will ye, I am sure, that you love me.

sentences.en: I am sure you will say that you love me.
sentences.ko: 당신도 저를 사랑한다고 말할 거라 확신해요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
If I do so, it will be of more price,
Being spoke behind your back than to your face.

sentences.en: If I do, it will be worth more behind your back than to your face.
sentences.ko: 그렇게 말한다면, 당신 앞에서 하는 것보다 뒤에서 하는 게 더 가치 있을 거예요.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Poor soul, thy face is much abus’d with tears.

sentences.en: Poor soul.
sentences.ko: 가엾은 사람.

sentences.en: Your face is badly hurt by tears.
sentences.ko: 눈물 때문에 얼굴이 많이 상했군요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
The tears have got small victory by that;
For it was bad enough before their spite.

sentences.en: The tears have won only a small victory.
sentences.ko: 눈물이 이긴 건 아주 작은 승리일 뿐이에요.

sentences.en: My face was ugly enough before they attacked it.
sentences.ko: 눈물이 닿기 전에도 제 얼굴은 충분히 못생겼거든요.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Thou wrong’st it more than tears with that report.

sentences.en: You insult your face more than the tears do by saying that.
sentences.ko: 그렇게 말하면 눈물보다 당신이 얼굴을 더 욕보이는 거예요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
That is no slander, sir, which is a truth,
And what I spake, I spake it to my face.

sentences.en: That is not a lie, sir, because it is the truth.
sentences.ko: 사실이니 거짓말이 아니지요.

sentences.en: And what I said, I said about my own face.
sentences.ko: 그리고 제가 한 말은 제 얼굴에 대한 것이었어요.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Thy face is mine, and thou hast slander’d it.

sentences.en: Your face is mine.
sentences.ko: 당신의 얼굴은 내 것이에요.

sentences.en: And you have insulted it.
sentences.ko: 그런데 당신이 그걸 모욕했네요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
It may be so, for it is not mine own.
Are you at leisure, holy father, now,
Or shall I come to you at evening mass?

sentences.en: It may be so, for it is not my own.
sentences.ko: 그럴지도 모르겠네요, 제 것이 아니니까요.

sentences.en: Are you free now, holy father?
sentences.ko: 신부님, 지금 시간 괜찮으신가요?

sentences.en: Or should I come to you at the evening mass?
sentences.ko: 아니면 저녁 미사 때 찾아뵈어야 할까요?

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
My leisure serves me, pensive daughter, now.—
My lord, we must entreat the time alone.

sentences.en: I am free now, my thoughtful daughter.
sentences.ko: 지금 괜찮다, 생각 깊은 딸아.

sentences.en: My lord, we must talk alone for a moment.
sentences.ko: 백작님, 잠시 둘이서만 이야기해야겠어요.

speaker: PARIS
raw:
God shield I should disturb devotion!—
Juliet, on Thursday early will I rouse ye,
Till then, adieu; and keep this holy kiss.

sentences.en: God forbid that I should disturb your prayers!
sentences.ko: 기도를 방해하다니 그럴 수는 없지요!

sentences.en: Juliet, I will wake you early on Thursday.
sentences.ko: 줄리엣, 목요일 아침 일찍 깨우러 올게요.

sentences.en: Until then, goodbye.
sentences.ko: 그때까지 안녕히.

sentences.en: And keep this holy kiss.
sentences.ko: 그리고 이 거룩한 입맞춤을 간직해요.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O shut the door, and when thou hast done so,
Come weep with me, past hope, past cure, past help!

sentences.en: Oh, shut the door and come to cry with me.
sentences.ko: 오, 문을 닫고 저와 함께 울어주세요.

sentences.en: My situation is hopeless; it cannot be cured, and no one can help me!
sentences.ko: 제 상황은 절망적이라 고칠 수 없고, 아무도 저를 도와줄 수 없어요!

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
O Juliet, I already know thy grief;
It strains me past the compass of my wits.
I hear thou must, and nothing may prorogue it,
On Thursday next be married to this County.

sentences.en: Juliet, I already know your grief.
sentences.ko: 줄리엣, 네 슬픔은 이미 알고 있다.

sentences.en: It is more than my mind can handle.
sentences.ko: 내 머리로는 어찌할 수가 없구나.

sentences.en: I hear that you must marry the Count.
sentences.ko: 네가 백작과 결혼해야 한다는 말을 들었다.

sentences.en: You must do it this coming Thursday.
sentences.ko: 이번 주 목요일에 결혼해야 한다고 말이다.

sentences.en: Nothing can stop it.
sentences.ko: 아무것도 막을 수 없다.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Tell me not, Friar, that thou hear’st of this,
Unless thou tell me how I may prevent it.
If in thy wisdom, thou canst give no help,
Do thou but call my resolution wise,
And with this knife I’ll help it presently.
God join’d my heart and Romeo’s, thou our hands;
And ere this hand, by thee to Romeo’s seal’d,
Shall be the label to another deed,
Or my true heart with treacherous revolt
Turn to another, this shall slay them both.
Therefore, out of thy long-experienc’d time,
Give me some present counsel, or behold
’Twixt my extremes and me this bloody knife
Shall play the empire, arbitrating that
Which the commission of thy years and art
Could to no issue of true honour bring.
Be not so long to speak. I long to die,
If what thou speak’st speak not of remedy.

sentences.en: Do not tell me about this, Friar, unless you tell me how I can stop it.
sentences.ko: 신부님, 제가 어떻게 막을 수 있는지 알려주지 않으실 거라면 이런 이야기는 하지 마세요.

sentences.en: If your wisdom gives no help, just call my decision wise.
sentences.ko: 신부님의 지혜로도 도울 수 없다면, 제 결심이 현명하다고만 해 주세요.

sentences.en: I will use this knife to help it right now.
sentences.ko: 그러면 지금 당장 이 칼로 해결하겠어요.

sentences.en: God joined my heart and Romeo's.
sentences.ko: 신께서 제 마음과 로미오의 마음을 묶어주셨어요.

sentences.en: You joined our hands.
sentences.ko: 신부님은 우리의 손을 묶어주셨고요.

sentences.en: This hand, which you joined to Romeo's, will never sign another marriage.
sentences.ko: 신부님이 로미오와 묶어주신 이 손은 결코 다른 결혼에 서명하지 않을 거예요.

sentences.en: It may try, or my true heart may betray him for another man.
sentences.ko: 이 손이 그러려 하거나, 제 마음이 그이를 배신하려 한다면요.

sentences.en: Then this knife will kill both hand and heart.
sentences.ko: 그러면 이 칼이 손과 마음을 모두 베어버릴 거예요.

sentences.en: Therefore, use your long experience.
sentences.ko: 그러니 신부님의 오랜 경험으로

sentences.en: Give me some immediate advice.
sentences.ko: 지금 당장 조언을 주세요.

sentences.en: If you cannot help, this bloody knife will judge between me and my terrible choice.
sentences.ko: 도울 수 없으시다면, 저와 제 끔찍한 처지 사이를 이 피 묻은 칼이 판가름할 거예요.

sentences.en: It will settle what your years and skill could not settle with honor.
sentences.ko: 신부님의 연륜과 지혜로도 명예롭게 풀지 못한 일을 이 칼이 끝낼 거예요.

sentences.en: Do not take a long time to speak.
sentences.ko: 말하는 데 오래 걸리지 마세요.

sentences.en: I long to die if what you say is not a cure.
sentences.ko: 신부님 말씀이 해결책이 아니라면 저는 죽고 싶어요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Hold, daughter. I do spy a kind of hope,
Which craves as desperate an execution
As that is desperate which we would prevent.
If, rather than to marry County Paris
Thou hast the strength of will to slay thyself,
Then is it likely thou wilt undertake
A thing like death to chide away this shame,
That cop’st with death himself to scape from it.
And if thou dar’st, I’ll give thee remedy.

sentences.en: Wait, daughter, for I see a kind of hope.
sentences.ko: 잠깐만, 내 딸아, 희망이 보이는구나.

sentences.en: It requires a desperate action, just as desperate as the one we want to prevent.
sentences.ko: 그건 우리가 막으려는 일만큼이나 절박한 행동을 필요로 한다.

sentences.en: You would rather kill yourself than marry Count Paris.
sentences.ko: 너는 패리스 백작과 결혼하느니 차라리 죽는 쪽을 택했지.

sentences.en: So you will likely dare to do something like death to escape this shame.
sentences.ko: 그러니 이 수치심에서 벗어나기 위해 죽음에 가까운 일을 감행할 수도 있겠구나.

sentences.en: You are ready to face death itself to escape it.
sentences.ko: 너는 이를 피하기 위해 죽음 그 자체에 맞설 준비가 되어 있다.

sentences.en: So if you dare, I will give you a remedy.
sentences.ko: 그러니 네가 용기를 낸다면, 내가 해결책을 주마.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O, bid me leap, rather than marry Paris,
From off the battlements of yonder tower,
Or walk in thievish ways, or bid me lurk
Where serpents are. Chain me with roaring bears;
Or hide me nightly in a charnel-house,
O’er-cover’d quite with dead men’s rattling bones,
With reeky shanks and yellow chapless skulls.
Or bid me go into a new-made grave,
And hide me with a dead man in his shroud;
Things that, to hear them told, have made me tremble,
And I will do it without fear or doubt,
To live an unstain’d wife to my sweet love.

sentences.en: Tell me to jump instead of marrying Paris.
sentences.ko: 패리스와 결혼하느니 차라리 뛰어내리라고 하세요.

sentences.en: I could jump from the walls of that tower over there.
sentences.ko: 저기 보이는 저 탑의 성벽에서 뛰어내릴 수도 있어요.

sentences.en: Or tell me to walk on roads full of thieves.
sentences.ko: 아니면 도둑이 우글거리는 길을 걸으라고 하세요.

sentences.en: Or I could hide where snakes are.
sentences.ko: 뱀들이 있는 곳에 숨으라고 하세요.

sentences.en: Chain me with roaring bears.
sentences.ko: 포효하는 곰들과 함께 묶어두세요.

sentences.en: Or hide me every night in a house for dead bodies.
sentences.ko: 아니면 매일 밤 납골당에 숨겨 주세요.

sentences.en: Cover me with dead men's rattling bones, stinking legs, and yellow jawless skulls.
sentences.ko: 죽은 자들의 덜컹거리는 뼈와 썩은 다리, 노란색의 턱 없는 해골들로 저를 덮어주세요.

sentences.en: Or tell me to go into a new grave.
sentences.ko: 아니면 새로운 무덤으로 가라고 말해주세요.

sentences.en: Hide me with a dead man in his shroud, the cloth that wraps the dead.
sentences.ko: 수의, 죽은 사람을 감싸는 천에 싸인 시체와 함께 숨겨 주세요.

sentences.en: These things make me tremble when I hear them.
sentences.ko: 이런 말들을 들으면 저는 몸이 떨려요.

sentences.en: But I will do them without fear or doubt.
sentences.ko: 하지만 두려움이나 의심 없이 그 일들을 할 거예요.

sentences.en: I will do them to stay a faithful, pure wife to my sweet love.
sentences.ko: 사랑하는 남편에게 흠 없는 아내로 남기 위해서라면요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Hold then. Go home, be merry, give consent
To marry Paris. Wednesday is tomorrow;
Tomorrow night look that thou lie alone,
Let not thy Nurse lie with thee in thy chamber.
Take thou this vial, being then in bed,
And this distilled liquor drink thou off,
When presently through all thy veins shall run
A cold and drowsy humour; for no pulse
Shall keep his native progress, but surcease.
No warmth, no breath shall testify thou livest,
The roses in thy lips and cheeks shall fade
To paly ashes; thy eyes’ windows fall,
Like death when he shuts up the day of life.
Each part depriv’d of supple government,
Shall stiff and stark and cold appear like death.
And in this borrow’d likeness of shrunk death
Thou shalt continue two and forty hours,
And then awake as from a pleasant sleep.
Now when the bridegroom in the morning comes
To rouse thee from thy bed, there art thou dead.
Then as the manner of our country is,
In thy best robes, uncover’d, on the bier,
Thou shalt be borne to that same ancient vault
Where all the kindred of the Capulets lie.
In the meantime, against thou shalt awake,
Shall Romeo by my letters know our drift,
And hither shall he come, and he and I
Will watch thy waking, and that very night
Shall Romeo bear thee hence to Mantua.
And this shall free thee from this present shame,
If no inconstant toy nor womanish fear
Abate thy valour in the acting it.

sentences.en: Wait then. Go home, be happy, and agree to marry Paris.
sentences.ko: 그럼 됐다. 집에 가서 즐거운 척하고, 패리스와 결혼하겠다고 해라.

sentences.en: Wednesday is tomorrow, so make sure you lie alone tomorrow night.
sentences.ko: 내일이 수요일이니, 내일 밤에는 혼자 누워 있어야 한다.

sentences.en: Do not let your Nurse stay in your room with you.
sentences.ko: 유모가 네 방에 함께 있게 해서는 안 된다.

sentences.en: Take this small bottle while you are in bed and drink all of this liquid.
sentences.ko: 침대에 누워서 이 작은 병을 꺼내 다 마셔라.

sentences.en: A cold and sleepy feeling will move through your veins until your pulse stops.
sentences.ko: 맥박이 멈출 때까지 차갑고 졸린 기운이 혈관을 타고 흐를 것이다.

sentences.en: No warmth or breath will show that you live.
sentences.ko: 네가 살아있다는 것을 보여주는 온기나 숨결은 나타나지 않을 것이다.

sentences.en: The color in your lips and cheeks will fade to gray.
sentences.ko: 입술과 뺨의 색은 회색으로 변할 것이다.

sentences.en: Your eyes will close as if death has closed the day of life.
sentences.ko: 마치 죽음이 생명의 날을 닫아버린 것처럼 네 눈이 감길 것이다.

sentences.en: Every part of you will become stiff and cold so you look like death.
sentences.ko: 네 몸의 모든 부분이 굳고 차가워져서 마치 죽은 것처럼 보일 것이다.

sentences.en: In this appearance of death, you will stay for forty-eight hours.
sentences.ko: 이 죽은 듯한 모습으로 너는 마흔여덟 시간 동안 머물게 될 것이다.

sentences.en: Then you will wake up as if from a pleasant sleep.
sentences.ko: 그러고 나서 마치 기분 좋은 잠에서 깨어난 것처럼 눈을 뜰 것이다.

sentences.en: When the groom comes in the morning to wake you, you will appear to be dead.
sentences.ko: 아침에 신랑이 너를 깨우러 올 때, 너는 죽은 것처럼 보일 것이다.

sentences.en: As our custom is, you will be dressed in your best clothes.
sentences.ko: 관습에 따라 너는 가장 좋은 옷을 입고 있을 것이다.

sentences.en: Your face will be uncovered on an open coffin.
sentences.ko: 열린 관 위에서 네 얼굴은 가려지지 않은 채 놓여 있을 것이다.

sentences.en: You will be carried to the old family vault, an underground tomb where all the Capulets lie.
sentences.ko: 너는 캐퓰릿 일족이 모두 잠든 지하 무덤인 오래된 가족 묘실로 옮겨질 것이다.

sentences.en: Before you wake up, Romeo will know our plan from my letters and he will come here.
sentences.ko: 네가 깨어나기 전에, 로미오는 내 편지를 통해 우리 계획을 알고 이곳으로 올 것이다.

sentences.en: He and I will watch you wake up, and that same night, Romeo will take you to Mantua.
sentences.ko: 그와 나는 네가 깨어나는 것을 지켜볼 것이고, 그날 밤 로미오는 너를 만토바로 데려갈 것이다.

sentences.en: This will free you from this shame if no silly whim or womanish fear weakens your courage.
sentences.ko: 어리석은 변덕이나 여자의 두려움이 네 용기를 약하게 만들지 않는다면, 이것이 너를 이 수치에서 구해줄 것이다.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Give me, give me! O tell not me of fear!

sentences.en: Give it to me, give it to me!
sentences.ko: 저에게 주세요, 저에게요!

sentences.en: Do not tell me about fear!
sentences.ko: 두려움에 대해 말씀하지 마세요!

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Hold; get you gone, be strong and prosperous
In this resolve. I’ll send a friar with speed
To Mantua, with my letters to thy lord.

sentences.en: Wait.
sentences.ko: 자, 받아라.

sentences.en: Go now.
sentences.ko: 이제 가거라.

sentences.en: Be strong and successful in this decision.
sentences.ko: 이 결심을 굳게 지키고 성공해라.

sentences.en: I will quickly send a friar to Mantua.
sentences.ko: 내가 곧바로 만토바에 신부를 보내겠다.

sentences.en: I will give him my letters for your lord.
sentences.ko: 네 남편에게 보내는 내 편지를 들려 보내마.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Love give me strength, and strength shall help afford.
Farewell, dear father.

sentences.en: Love, give me strength, because strength will provide what I need.
sentences.ko: 사랑이여, 제게 힘을 주세요. 그 힘이 저를 도울 거예요.

sentences.en: Goodbye, dear father.
sentences.ko: 안녕히 계세요, 신부님.

raw: Exeunt.
